title: The Little Book Workshop
physical_metaphor: A single paper project folio unfolds into three color-coded job pieces—a cover, page stack and binding strip—which three Motif Bots work on simultaneously, then physically assemble into one finished book and deliver forward.
visual_story: A front-on tabletop film in warm paper, ink and teal with marigold accents. The same <> project seal appears first on the closed folio, then across its three distributed pieces, and finally recombines on the finished book cover. At 3–10 seconds, a locked wide composition shows all three Bots genuinely working at once: one feeds and folds the cover through a simple crease jig, one presses a loose page stack flat, and one carries the binding strip toward the center. Their distinct silhouettes and persistent colors keep every component traceable. The completed parts arrive together, slot into place with one firm press, and become a readable finished book. A Bot carries it forward and places it into waiting paper hands at the bottom of frame.
audience_script: One project opens into three independent jobs. While one Bot folds the cover, another presses the pages, and a third brings the binding. Their finished pieces meet, lock together, and the complete book arrives in your hands.

beats.subject: 0:00–0:03 — Sealed project folio and three Motif Bots
beats.physical_action: The lead Bot pulls the <> tab; the folio unfolds into three attached job pieces, which slide along short tabletop lanes into three waiting Bot grips.
beats.before_after: One compact sealed project becomes a marigold cover sheet, cream page stack and teal binding strip, each retaining one-third of the <> seal.
beats.consequence: The three Bots receive distinct components and begin work together.
beats.framing_intent: Start close on the clear project seal, then widen enough to reveal all three destinations in one shallow tabletop view.

beats.subject: 0:03–0:10 — Cover, pages and binding strip
beats.physical_action: In one sustained wide shot, Bot one feeds the cover into a hinged crease jig and folds it; Bot two lowers both mittens to press the uneven pages into a neat block; Bot three carries the curled binding strip across the table toward the assembly cradle. Actions overlap with staggered anticipation and weighted settles.
beats.before_after: Flat cover gains a spine fold; splayed pages become a squared stack; distant curled binding arrives straightened at the shared assembly point.
beats.consequence: Three independently finished pieces become ready at nearly the same moment.
beats.framing_intent: Use three strong side-by-side silhouettes with no camera hopping; crop tightly enough that folding, compression and travel remain legible at mobile size.

beats.subject: 0:10–0:14 — Three finished components in the assembly cradle
beats.physical_action: The cover wraps around the arriving page block, the binding strip slides over the spine, and all three Bots press once together.
beats.before_after: Three separate colored pieces become one bound book; the divided seal aligns into a complete <> mark on its cover.
beats.consequence: The shared press produces the finished deliverable and gives the Bots a clear object to hand off.
beats.framing_intent: Move to a centered medium close view where the aligning seal and locking spine are the smallest essential details.

beats.subject: 0:14–0:18 — Finished <> project book
beats.physical_action: Two Bots lift the book onto the carrier Bot's open mittens. The carrier steps forward, extends the book, and releases it into two waiting paper hands entering from below.
beats.before_after: The deliverable moves from workshop ownership to the viewer's hands while remaining visibly the same completed book.
beats.consequence: Parallel work resolves as one tangible, physically delivered result.
beats.framing_intent: Keep the complete cover, seal and receiving hands unobstructed; end on a brief still hold rather than a celebration bounce.

new_assets.purpose: A fold-out folio that separates into a cover sheet, page stack and binding strip while preserving a divided project seal.
new_assets.reusable_interaction: Open, unfold, distribute, separate and recombine modular project pieces.

new_assets.purpose: A pair of broad paper boards that visibly folds a sheet without becoming a detailed machine.
new_assets.reusable_interaction: Feed, hinge, crease and release cards, covers or packaging.

new_assets.purpose: Two simple rounded plates that compress an uneven stack into a tidy block.
new_assets.reusable_interaction: Press, flatten, align or stamp stacked materials.

new_assets.purpose: A shallow U-shaped guide that holds components while they slot together.
new_assets.reusable_interaction: Receive, align, join and release modular parts.

new_assets.purpose: A pair of large open paper mitts at the foreground edge for physical delivery to the audience.
new_assets.reusable_interaction: Receive books, parcels, cards or other finished deliverables.

reuse: Locked Motif Bot v1 duplicated three times with canonical grip, open and mitten hand states
Existing warm paper palette, restrained marigold accent, matte grain and down-right shadows
Existing wall, floor and shallow desk environment
Existing fold, slide, carry, press, handoff and short settle motion language
Canonical <> identity mark as the persistent project seal
limits: The book metaphor clearly shows independent components joining into one deliverable, but real project jobs may exchange information or depend on one another before final assembly.
The three-way split is a deliberately simple example; it does not imply every project divides evenly or benefits from exactly three workers.
Simultaneous tabletop actions communicate concurrency visually, not precise timing, workload or performance gains.
The reusable jigs are finite paper interactions, not a proposal for a detailed machine system or a broader prop library.
